steps.why: The word milk describes the appearance. Calcium hydroxide dissolves only slightly in water, so most of it stays as solid particles held in the liquid and the mixture looks white.
common_mistakes: Calling it a solution. It is a suspension, because calcium hydroxide is only slightly soluble.
Confusing it with milk of magnesia. Milk of lime is Ca(OH)₂ in water; milk of magnesia is Mg(OH)₂ in water.
steps.memory_tip: Lime means calcium, so milk of lime is calcium hydroxide in water.
steps.margin_note: Write the formula Ca(OH)₂ beside the name.

steps.why: Milk of lime is only slaked lime and water, so the answer is complete once the reaction that makes slaked lime is written and one or two uses are named.
common_mistakes: Writing quick lime, CaO, as milk of lime. Quick lime is the oxide, while milk of lime holds the hydroxide.
Writing lime water instead. Lime water is the clear saturated solution of calcium hydroxide; milk of lime is the thick white suspension.
steps.memory_tip: Quick lime plus water gives slaked lime, and slaked lime with more water gives milk of lime.
steps.margin_note: One equation and one named use complete this answer.

insider_note: The answer is short: name the suspension, give the formula Ca(OH)₂, and add the reaction that makes slaked lime.
